payload.title: pdfExtractorClient Tier-1 120s OCR timeout too short -> silent BCTC reflow failure
payload.problem: Tier-1 extraction call hardcodes AbortSignal.timeout(120_000). OCR of medium/large scanned Vietnamese BCTC PDFs (e.g. HPG Q4-2025 consolidated, 33 pages) exceeds 120s (a direct 480s call to pdf-extractor:5001/extract still did not return; tesseract ran 17+ min continuously). All 3 tiers then fail, but silently: push-bctc-pdf returns {ok:true}, bctc_vps_queue row is marked done (attempts=1), yet financial_reports scalars are left stale with NO error surfaced.
payload.impact: Any push-bctc-pdf ingestion whose OCR exceeds 120s silently leaves financial_reports stale. Concretely blocks the HPG Q4-2025 consolidated data-coverage-gap closure: queue row 223 source_url IS corrected to the consolidated hop-nhat PDF and the file IS on disk (7135524B), but financial_reports row 918a7abd-... still holds the standalone rieng scalars.
payload.recommended: Bump Tier-1 timeout to an OCR-realistic value, OR re-route large PDFs through the async /api/trigger-pek-extract path instead of the synchronous 3-tier gauntlet. Design choice (bump vs async re-route) -> PO/architect triage. Implementation needs a container rebuild (deploy-gated).
payload.reflow_reset_note: After the fix ships + mcp-server rebuild, reset bctc_vps_queue row 223 (HPG 2025 Q4) status done->pending to re-trigger the consolidated reflow. It is currently 'done' from the silent-failure path, so it will NOT auto-reparse without an explicit reset.
